### Observed differences

- The execution order between A01 and the pair A06/A07 reversed. In the earlier window, A06 and then A07 always ran before A01 (in all 200 traced cases); in the later window, A01 always ran before both (again in all 200 cases), while the two activities still always occurred together in each case. [REL001, REL002]
- Successor relations changed accordingly: A08 led to A06 in all observed outgoing transitions before and leads to A01 in all after; A01, from which no outgoing transition was observed before (it was the final step), now always leads to A06; A07, which previously led to A01, now has no observed outgoing transition (it is now the final step). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- Distances from A08 shifted consistently: A08→A01 shortened from 3 steps to 1, A08→A06 lengthened from 1 to 2, and A08→A07 from 2 to 3, each in all 200 cases. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- Event positions moved in the same direction: A01's mean position fell from 1.0 to about 0.71 (normalised), A06's rose from about 0.71 to about 0.86, and A07's rose from about 0.86 to 1.0. [POS001, POS002, POS003]
- Participation was unchanged: A01, A06 and A07 each appear in all 200 traces in both windows, and A08 anchors the segment in all cases throughout. [POS001, POS002, POS003, DIR003, LAG001]
- Screening context: 11 control-flow items qualified, where roughly 0.05 would be expected if nothing had changed, and each difference exceeded that seen in about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled traces. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the closing segment of the process was reordered with respect to A01: in the earlier window the segment ran A08 → A06 → A07 → A01, with A01 last, while in the later window it runs A08 → A01 → A06 → A07, with A01 executed immediately after A08 and A07 now last. In behavioural terms, A06 and A07 moved from preceding A01 to following it. [REL001, REL002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, POS001, POS002, POS003]

The supporting signs are direct and consistent: the order reversal is shown relationally in 200 of 200 co-occurrence cases in each window; the successor, distance and position items all describe one and the same permutation; every involved activity still occurs in all traces in both windows, so this is a reordering rather than activities being added, removed or skipped; and the qualified item count (11 versus about 0.05 expected without change) far exceeds what an unchanged process typically produces. [REL001, REL002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, POS001, POS002, POS003]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a reordering within every trace from a drastic shift in the mix of two pre-existing variants (one ending A06→A07→A01, the other A01→A06→A07), because each window shows only a single order; the empty direction profiles only mean no outgoing transition was observed in that window, not that an edge is absent; and the position indicator uses event positions rather than clock time, though the relational and successor evidence shows the order change directly. [DIR001, DIR002, REL001, REL002, POS001]

Other differences: none — every qualified item describes this single reordering of A01, A06, A07 and A08. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
